**Root cause: a malformed pricing rule is crashing the engine at startup — this is NOT a Kubernetes problem.**

**Evidence:**
Both pods (`pricing-engine-74d9c6b8f-5tnwh` and `pricing-engine-74d9c6b8f-jq7lc`) show identical panics in their logs immediately after startup:

```
INFO fetched 1,204 active rules from rules-admin (revision 8841)
INFO compiling rule BF-2026-STACKED (tiers=3, stacking=true)
panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3
  github.com/acme/pricing/internal/rules.(*TierTable).Lookup … tiers.go:88
```

The engine starts, fetches rules from `rules-admin` at **revision 8841**, then immediately panics with an off-by-one error while compiling rule **`BF-2026-STACKED`**. The `TierTable.Lookup` call tries to access index 3 in a 3-element (0-indexed) array — a classic off-by-one. The process exits with **code 2**, triggering the `CrashLoopBackOff` Kubernetes shows (12 restarts on each pod) [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1].

Because the engine crashes during its startup compilation phase every time, Kubernetes applies exponential back-off and keeps retrying [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-0]. Kubernetes itself is behaving correctly; the problem is entirely in the rule data.

**Why it started at ~2 pm today despite no deployment:** The pricing-engine image hasn't changed (deployed 2026-04-27), but the engine fetches rules live from `rules-admin` on every startup. Someone must have added or modified rule **`BF-2026-STACKED`** in `rules-admin` around 2 pm today, pushing it to revision 8841. That bad rule is what's crashing the engine.

**Fix (no Kubernetes changes needed):**
1. Open the `pricing-rules-admin` UI (pod `pricing-rules-admin-6b8f7d5c9-wd3pk` is healthy and running).
2. Find rule **`BF-2026-STACKED`** — it is configured with `tiers=3, stacking=true` but has a tier table with only 3 entries (indices 0–2). The compiler tries to look up index 3, which doesn't exist.
3. Either **correct the tier table** so it contains a 4th entry (index 3), or **disable/delete the rule** if it was added in error.
4. Once the rule data is fixed, the pricing-engine pods will be able to complete their startup compilation and will come healthy automatically on the next restart cycle — no redeployment of the engine image is required [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-2].
